parsed.narrative: With the default choices, religiosity goes with higher well-being: beta = 0.140 (95% CI 0.119 to 0.160), p < 0.001, n = 10,535, so the verdict is POSITIVE ASSOCIATION. Borges ran 40 universes: the baseline, 13 single changes and 26 combinations. No flip was found: all 40 universes keep the verdict (robustness 100%); the estimate runs from 0.064 to 0.150, the lowest interval bound is 0.035 and the largest p-value is p < 0.001. The 110 research teams that reported a standardised effect range from 0.007 to 0.354 (median 0.120), and 110 of them (100%) have an interval above zero.
caveats: The share of universes that agree is a property of the explored set, which is built from the choices the teams documented and searched for flips; it is not a population estimate.
Standardised coefficients describe an association in a convenience sample of 24 countries; they do not show that religion causes well-being.
